THE AIRPORT SECURITY FORCE (SERVICE) RULES, 1978
THE AIRPORT SECURITY FORCE (SERVICE) RULES,
1978
[20th April, 1978]
S.R.O. 433(1) 78.-In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 11
of the Airport Security Force Act, 1975 (LXXVII of 1975), the Federal
Government is pleased to make the following rules, namely:‑
1. Short title, commencement and application.--(1) These rules may
be called the Officers and Members of the Airports Security Force (Service)
Rules, 1978.
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
(3) They shall apply to all
officers and members wherever they may be.
2. Definitions.--In these rules, unless, there is anything
repugnant in the subject or context,-
(a) "Act"
means the Airports Security Force Act, 1975 (LXXVII of 1975);
(b) "Grade"
means the National Scale of Pay in which a post or group of posts is placed;
and
(c) "Unit"
means a detachment of the Force entrusted with the responsibility of Security
of an Airport.
3. Headquarters of the Force.--(1) The headquarters of the Force
shall be at such place as the Federal Government may by order appoint.
(2) The Units may be posted at
such airports as the Federal Government may by order in writing direct.
4. General supervision of the Director-General.--The Force
Commander shall exercise his powers and perform his function under the general
supervision of the Director-General who:-
(a) shall be
responsible to the Federal Government for the administration of the Force in
accordance with the Act and any rules, orders or instructions made at issued by
that Government from time to time
(b) shall
exercise all financial powers relating to it; and may, from time to time, issue
such directions to the Force Commander and officers as he thinks necessary.
5. Duties of the Force Commander.--The Force Commander shall be the
administrative head of the Force and:-
(a) shall be in
command and control of the Force;
(b) shall be
responsible to the Director-General in respect of all matters concerning the
Force and the exercise of his administrative functions under Section 5 of the
Act;
(c) may, by
general or special order, assign duties to the officers and members;
(d) shall be
responsible for the maintenance of its discipline; and
(e) shall take
such measures for the training of its officers and members as are necessary.
6. Duties of officers and members.-- All officers and members of
the Force shall comply with the orders of their superior officers and perform
such duties as may from time to time be assigned to them by the Force
Commander.
7. Assistant Director to be Chief Security Officer.-- An Assistant
Director appointed to a Unit shall be the Chief Security Officer of the airport
at which the Unit is posted, and
(a) shall be
responsible to the Force Commander in respect of all matters concerning his
Unit, including the discipline and training of its officers and members;
(b) shall be in
command in control of his Unit; and
(c) may, by
general or special order, assign duties to -officers and members of his Unit:
8. Composition of the Force.--The Force shall consist of the
following, officers and members with the designation and grades shown each
namely:-
(i) Force
Commander in Grade 19 or 20.
(ii) Deputy
Directors in Grade 18 plus a special pay of Rs. 150 per month.
(iii) Assistant
Directors in Grade 18.
(iv) Security
Officers in Grade 17.
(v) Assistant
Security Officers in Grade 16.
(vi) Inspectors
in Grade 11.
(vii) Sub-Inspectors
in Grade 7.
(viii) Assistant
Sub-Inspectors in Grade 5.
(ix) Drivers in
Grade 5.
(x) Guards Class
-I in Grade 3.
(xi) Guards
Class-II in Grade 2.
9. Authority to make appointments.--(1) The authority competent to
make appointment in the Force to Grade 17 and above shall be the Adviser for
the Establishment Division.
(2) The authority competent to
make appointments in the Force to Grade 1 to 15 shall be the Force Commander.
